processing_steps.atmosphere: high vacuum (pressure below 10^-6 bar) then high-purity argon (pressure below 1 bar)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Raw materials (>99.8 wt% pure) placed in a water-cooled copper crucible; melting repeated at least five times to promote chemical homogeneity and reduce gas contamination; average interstitial contents of the process are O (12–89 ppm), N (~18 ppm) and H (~2 ppm). Zr0.01 steel is Fe-25Mn-7Al-0.9C-0.01Zr (wt%).
Applied to the as-cast steels; Fig. S1 shows that oxygen segregation to grain boundaries does not occur.
Hot-rolling with a thickness reduction of 40 %, followed by water quenching.
The hot-rolled plates were subjected to cold rolling with an 80 % reduction; heavy cold rolling introduces micro shear bands.
Short-time annealing at 900 °C for 5 min followed by water-quenching; this is the terminal state prior to tensile deformation.

structures.overall_structure: Prior to tensile deformation, the Zr0.01 steel shows an essentially homogeneous, fully recrystallized FCC grain structure of predominantly coarse equiaxed grains (average 7 μm), with randomly oriented grains and low KAM values; only a small fraction of fine FCC grains (~7 %) is present, so a mild heterogeneous feature begins to appear but the structure is described as homogeneous (like Zr0).
structures.microstructure_counts: Coarse grain fraction ~93% (just above 90%); fine grain fraction ~7% (Fig. 3a).

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed recrystallized grains; predominantly coarse grains with only a few fine grains
phases_present.grain_size: 7 μm (average FCC grain size for the Zr0.01 steel)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: unimodal, peak near 5–6 μm with a tail extending to ~17 μm (Fig. 3c)

microstructure_list.region: fine FCC grain (FG) zones (minor fraction within the matrix)

phases_present.volume_fraction: ~7% (fine grain fraction of the Zr0.01 steel, Fig. 3a)

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: flat dog-bone-shaped samples with a gauge length of 14 mm and width of 4 mm, prepared from the cold-rolled plate along the rolling direction (RD)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Uniaxial tensile testing using an Instron 5892 machine; experimental data recorded via a contact extensometer.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–strain curve of the Zr0.01 steel shown in Fig. 4a (red curve); peaks between 800 and 1000 MPa with fracture between 0.5 and 0.6 engineering strain.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: tensile properties: yield strength (~435 vs ~450 MPa), ultimate tensile strength (820 vs ~832 MPa), fracture ductility (52% vs 55%)

characterization_methods.purpose: reveal the microstructure of the Fe-Mn-Al-C steels with different Zr content before deformation
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the Zr0.01 steel the microstructure consists of coarse FCC grains and few fine FCC grains (Fig. 1b).

characterization_methods.technique: electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) — inverse pole figure (IPF), image quality (IQ) and kernel average misorientation (KAM) maps
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM equipped with an EBSD detector (accelerating voltage: 30 kV, step size: 500 nm)
characterization_methods.purpose: reveal microstructure evolution, grain size and grain orientation of the steels
characterization_methods.key_findings: Compared with Zr0, the average size of recrystallized FCC grains in the Zr0.01 steel is obviously reduced and grain orientations are random (Fig. 2b–b2); the KAM map is predominantly dark blue (low misorientation) with only faint, sparse green speckles, indicating a low dislocation density (recrystallized state).
The fracture surface of the Zr0.01 steel shows equiaxed dimples that appear somewhat coarser than in the Zr0 steel (Fig. 4c).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, strain rate 10^-3 s^-1, flat dog-bone specimen (gauge length 14 mm, width 4 mm), RD
characterization_methods.purpose: measure the mechanical properties of the Zr0.01 steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: Yield strength ~450 MPa, ultimate tensile strength ~832 MPa, fracture ductility 55 %.

unmapped_findings: The Zr0.01 steel is a comparison/benchmark material in this study; the quantitative strengthening and thermodynamic analyses (HDI + grain-boundary strengthening ~300 MPa, ZrC precipitation strengthening 108 MPa, critical twinning stress ~1.14 GPa, and the Thermo-Calc ZrC phase-fraction ~0.6 % at 900 °C) are reported only for the Zr0.50 steel, i.e. they do not belong to the Zr0.01 sample.

ZrC carbides are present in the Zr-alloyed steels, but their fraction is stated to be highest in the Zr0.50 steel and lower in the Zr0.01 steel; no ZrC size or fraction is quantified for the Zr0.01 sample.

During steelmaking (applied to all three steels including Zr0.01) the average interstitial contents achieved were O (12–89 ppm), N (~18 ppm) and H (~2 ppm), and Fig. S1 shows that oxygen segregation to grain boundaries does not occur.
